correctness.rationale: The cumulative monitor integral inverts to e^{-lambda p t_j}=(nu+N-j)/(nu+N); subtraction yields h_j=H(nu+N-j-1)/(lambda p). The positive Laplace mixture representation of H gives strict log-convexity (variance >0), hence F(x)=H(x)/H(x+1) strictly decreases from infinity to 1. This proves ordering, uniqueness, threshold equivalence and strict integer rounding for all admissible inputs, not merely sampled cases. The exact standalone verifier performs 1,296 high-precision comparisons including independent node inversion, ratio checks, boundary decisions and asymptotics.

value.rationale: A design conflict arises when energy-rate equidistribution is used with a fixed maximum neighboring-step ratio. The exact sharp number of mesh intervals required to satisfy both restrictions is a motivated planning quantity, not an arbitrary example: for exponential relaxation it scales as D under the energy-rate monitor but only sqrt(D) under the square-root monitor. The single universal transcendental root of R gives the complete classification for every horizon, monitor exponent and strict cap, including equality cases. The result quantifies why the square-root alternative can avoid aggressive grid-ratio clamping at substantially lower mesh cost, without asserting an implementation-level performance theorem.
